questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to build a self-driving car
The belief that technology is always the best solution
Why computers will soon be smarter than people in every way
The history of artificial intelligence
questions.why: The topic is technochauvinism, 'the idea that technology is always the highest and best solution'.

questions.q: What does Rob think about self-driving cars?
options: They will be more dangerous than human drivers
They will never be allowed on roads
They will be safer but take away the fun of driving
They are only useful for long journeys
questions.why: Rob says they'll be safer than humans but will take away some of the pleasure of driving.

questions.q: What does Rob say 'better' depends on?
options: What you mean by 'better'
How much the technology costs
Who made the technology
How fast it works
questions.why: Rob says 'I guess it depends on what you mean by better.'

questions.q: According to Meredith Broussard, what have we got into the habit of thinking?
options: Computers are too expensive
People are better than machines
Technology is making us lazy and less able to think for ourselves
Using a computer is always the best and fairest way
questions.why: She says we think doing something with a computer is 'the best and most objective way', which isn't true.

questions.q: Why does Broussard say computers are not objective?
options: They make lots of mistakes
They reflect the people who make them
They can be hacked easily
They don't have enough data
questions.why: She says computers 'are proxies for the people who make them'.

questions.q: Why does Broussard say there is no such thing as perfect data?
options: The world has problems like racism and sexism
Because computers are too slow
Because data is always out of date by the time it is used
Because people lie in surveys
questions.why: She says we have data on the world as it is, with serious problems of racism, sexism and more.

questions.q: What problem does Broussard see inside the tech world?
options: There are too few programmers to build all the technology we need
Tech companies earn too much
Algorithm creators don't understand social issues well
Algorithms are too simple
questions.why: She says creators of algorithms 'do not have sufficient awareness of social issues'.

questions.q: What does Catherine suggest listeners think about next time they use an app?
options: Whether it is free
How fast it works
Whether it has good reviews from lots of other users
Whether it reflects its developers' views
questions.why: She says you might wonder if it contains nuances 'that reflect the views of the developer'.
